rancho: Rancho Cucamonga, San Bernardino County, California
disambiguation: This is the SAN BERNARDINO COUNTY Rancho Cucamonga: a 13,045-acre Mexican land grant made in 1839 by Gov. Juan Bautista Alvarado to Tiburcio Tapia, in present-day City of Rancho Cucamonga (villages of Cucamonga, Alta Loma, Etiwanda). Ownership chain: Tiburcio Tapia (1839) -> daughter Maria Merced Tapia and husband Leon Victor Prudhomme (patent issued to Prudhomme, 1872) -> John Rains and Maria Merced Williams de Rains (purchased 1858, built the brick Casa/Rains House 1860-61) -> later owners; George and William Chaffey developed the adjacent Etiwanda/Ontario irrigation colonies from 1881 on former rancho-region land. NOT to be confused with any similarly named Southern California place; this is distinct from the Orange County city 'Rancho Santa Margarita' and from Malibu's Tapia family lands (Rancho Topanga Malibu Sequit). All items below depict San Bernardino County land unless flagged.
visual_record_note: The cattle-operation era of this rancho (Tapia 1839-1858; Rains 1858-1864) predates local photography. Tiburcio Tapia's adobe on Red Hill was abandoned in 1858 and disintegrated; no photographs of it or of the Tapia/Rains cattle operation are known to survive. The surviving visual record is therefore (a) 19th-century manuscript survey/subdivision maps (Huntington Solano-Reeve collection), (b) photographs of the surviving brick Rains House / Casa de Rancho Cucamonga (built 1860-61), and (c) later wine-industry photographs. This is a land-use image archive; no contamination claim is made.

physical_only_collections: Rancho Cucamonga Library Services (Archibald Library), 10500 Civic Center Drive, Rancho Cucamonga, CA 91730; (909) 477-2720; reference@cityofrc.us. Holds the 'Collection of City of Rancho Cucamonga Local History Photographs' (circa 1897-1980; ~200 items: photographs, maps, wine labels, records documenting the Virginia Dare / Thomas / Cucamonga wineries, agriculture, buildings, city views, floods, early residents). Collection is stored offsite at a remote storage facility; advance notice required for access. Only a subset is digitized on Calisphere/OAC (finding aid ark:/13030/kt0z09r4gs); rights: 'Property rights reside with the City of Rancho Cucamonga Library.'

San Bernardino County Museum -- Maria Merced Williams & John Rains House (Casa de Rancho Cucamonga), 8810 Hemlock St, Rancho Cucamonga, CA 91730 (branch of the San Bernardino County Museum, 2024 Orange Tree Lane, Redlands, CA 92374; (909) 307-2669). On-site interpretive/historic-house collection for the 1860-61 rancho brick house (NRHP #73000428). Historic images likely held on site / by the Casa de Rancho Cucamonga Historical Society.

California State Polytechnic University, Pomona -- Special Collections & Archives, University Library, 3801 W. Temple Ave, Pomona, CA 91768; (909) 869-3775; speccollections@cpp.edu. Holds the 'Southern California Wine and Wine Industry Photograph Collection, circa 1890-2013' (8.04 lin. ft.) incl. Cucamonga-region wineries (e.g., Virginia Dare Winery in Rancho Cucamonga), plus the Pomona Valley Historical Collection. Advance notice required; some items digitized. Rights: permission to publish must be secured from repository and copyright holder.

California State Archives, 1020 O Street, Sacramento, CA 95814; (916) 653-2246; ArchivesWeb@sos.ca.gov. U.S. Surveyor General Maps series includes the Rancho Cucamonga grant plat; reproduction on request.

The Bancroft Library, UC Berkeley -- 'Land Case Files' (collection 12346) for the Rancho Cucamonga private land claim (Prudhomme claimant, patented 1872). The case file / any surviving diseno was not found digitized on Calisphere this session; an on-site or finding-aid check is warranted.
dead_ends: Library of Congress HABS/HAER: no Historic American Buildings Survey record found for the Casa de Rancho Cucamonga / John Rains House (loc.gov json search 'Casa de Rancho Cucamonga' and 'Rancho Cucamonga Rains' returned only tangential items -- e.g. the unrelated 'Goerlitz House' HABS ca2330 in Rancho Cucamonga, Pomona Valley histories, newspapers). The Rains House is on the National Register (#73000428) but does not appear to have a digitized HABS set at LOC.

Bancroft Library 'Maps of private land grant cases of California' (Calisphere collection 12347): no diseno or land-case map titled Cucamonga surfaced. Every 'Cucamonga' map hit on Calisphere resolves to the Huntington Solano-Reeve collection, not a Bancroft diseno. The Cucamonga grant appears to have been confirmed via the Prudhomme claim/U.S. survey rather than a digitized surviving diseno.

David Rumsey Historical Map Collection (LUNA API, q=Cucamonga): only 3 tangential hits -- 'Ontario. Detail Irrigation Map.', an irrigation-history chapter map, and a 'Wine Map of California' -- none is a Rancho-Cucamonga-specific ranch/land map.

Huntington Digital Library Photographs collection (p15150coll2), dmQuery title contains 'Cucamonga': 0 records. The Huntington's Cucamonga holdings are maps (Solano-Reeve, 22 records), not photographs.

USC Digital Library and UCLA Library Special Collections: no Rancho Cucamonga ranch-specific photograph or map surfaced via web search (only general landing pages and the Cal Poly Pomona wine collection).

BLM GLO Records detail pages (survey dm_id / patent accession for Cucamonga): pages are JavaScript/ASP.NET-rendered and returned identical shell HTML to curl and 401/403 to WebFetch; specific accession numbers (22286 / CACAAA 081621 / dm_id 288883) came from search-index snippets and could NOT be independently confirmed this session.

vredenburgh.org California GLO/BLM Land Patents table (to verify the Cucamonga patent accession): server returned HTTP 500; could not confirm the exact GLO document number for the Prudhomme/Cucamonga patent.

Calisphere item pages are client-side (React) rendered and return 0 bytes to curl and empty content to WebFetch; item metadata was obtained via the underlying ContentDM dmwebservices API (Huntington, LAPL) and via OAC finding aids / search snippets instead.

No photographs of the Tapia/Rains CATTLE operation or the original Tiburcio Tapia adobe (Red Hill) are known to exist: the adobe was abandoned in 1858 and disintegrated, and the cattle era (1839-1864) predates local photography. Guasti / Italian Vineyard Company imagery (e.g. Calisphere e4af6b8a) was EXCLUDED as it depicts Guasti (present-day Ontario area), which is adjacent to but not on the Tapia Rancho Cucamonga grant proper -- flagged to avoid conflation.
